title: Day 16 · Foundation: Net force from diagrams
c1: Add forces on a level floor
q1: On page 61, take right as positive. Use the two horizontal forces to find the net force and acceleration of the box. Show both steps and give directions.
q2: Use the 2 kg block and 30° ramp on page 62. Assume no friction. The ramp rises to the right. Draw only weight and normal force with the sizes shown. Measure arrow angles counterclockwise from horizontal right.
q3: Now include friction. A 2 kg block has a downhill weight component of 9.8 N and uphill friction of 4.0 N. Find its net force along the ramp and its acceleration. Explain why you did not add the full weight again.
q4: On page 64 a student subtracts the size of downward gravity from sideways thrust. Check this method. Describe how you would find the direction of the net force instead.
q5: On your own: a 10 kg box is pushed forward with 50 N. Friction is 15 N backward. Find the net force and acceleration. A different cart moves backward with forward acceleration. Does that cart speed up or slow down at first? Explain.
a1: Subtract 10 N from 30 N to get 20 N right. Divide by 5 kg to get 4 m/s² right.
a2: Draw Earth’s pull at 270° with size 19.6 N. Draw the ramp’s support at 120° with size about 17 N. The dashed weight components are for calculation.
a3: Downhill is positive. The sum is 9.8 − 4.0 = 5.8 N downhill. Divide by 2 kg to get 2.9 m/s² downhill. The component already includes the along-ramp effect of weight.
a4: The forces lie on different axes. Add the components on each axis or draw the vectors tip to tail. The net points both sideways and down.
a5: The net is 35 N forward. The acceleration is 3.5 m/s² forward. Backward motion slows at first because acceleration points forward.
